content: # Miracle of Kaiserslautern: The Only Promoted Team to Win the Bundesliga. In Bundesliga history, only one has become the sole story of an unspeakable championship victory by a newly promoted team. FC Kaiserslautern in the 1997-98 season. Among all of Bundesliga history, Kaiserslautern stands alone as the only team to have won the championship right after promotion and become a permanent member of the football legend. Kaiserslautern’s football club received its most significant setback when the team lost to the 2. Before coming to Kaiserslautern, Otto Rehhagel obtained distinction in German football by leading Werder Bremen to win the Bundesliga in 1992. The 1996-97 Bundesliga season introduced Kaiserslautern to an unexpected championship pathway that would create one of German history’s most unimaginable football triumphs. The Bundesliga victory achieved by Kaiserslautern during 1997-98 represents one of the most legendary narratives in football history.

title: The most unlikely Bundesliga winners of all - DW News
content: But 22 years ago, they shot up from the second tier to win the Bundesliga at the first go, crushing Bayern Munich on the way. If Otto Rehhagel hoped to carry some of the momentum from his team's march to the 1996-97 Bundesliga 2 title in to a daunting season in Germany's top flight, he was dealt an early blow when the fixture list came out. His revenge was first swift — as an 80th-minute goal from Michael Schjonberg secured the newly-promoted side a shock win on the opening day — then deep, with Kaiserslautern briefly breaking Bayern and Borussia Dortmund's decade-long duopoly with a title win forged on that first day. The side from a town with a population of less than 100,000 in the south-west of Germany drew an average gate of 36,709 to the Fritz Walter stadium in their victorious 2.Bundesliga campaign, with the name of their ground a nod to their rich history —Walter was captain of the West Germany side that pulled off one of the biggest shocks in World Cup history in 1954.

content: # Kaiserslautern: The Only Team to Win the Bundesliga Right After Promotion. Kaiserslautern: The Only Team to Win the Bundesliga Right After Promotion. In 1998, newly-promoted Kaiserslautern achieved the impossible: winning the Bundesliga in their first season back in the top flight. In 1998, newly-promoted Kaiserslautern achieved the impossible: winning the Bundesliga in their first season back in the top flight. In 1996-97, Kaiserslautern dominated the second division, winning promotion at the first attempt with a squad that was largely unchanged from the team that had been relegated. Kaiserslautern had done what no promoted team had ever done before – they had won the Bundesliga in their first season back. Today, promoted teams face opponents with vastly superior resources, making it almost impossible to sustain a title challenge over an entire season. The same is true in other major leagues – promoted teams occasionally surprise with good seasons, but winning the league immediately? Kaiserslautern didn't just win the Bundesliga – they made history.

title: The German Leicester... how Kaiserslautern shocked the Bundesliga in 1998 | Football News | Sky Sports
content: #### Premier League. #### Women's Super League. In recent months, Leicester's 5,000/1 Premier League title charge has drawn only a handful of parallels from English football's modern era. The story of Kaiserslautern's 1997/98 Bundesliga win is one less told, but just as unprecedented. Having risen from the second division under footballing miracle-worker Otto Rehhagel in 1997, Kaiserslautern became the only Bundesliga team to win the title after being promoted the previous season. Their success was unthinkable given the mid-90s dominance of Bayern Munich and Borussia Dortmund, but Rehhagel's first of two major career turn-ups was a masterstroke. Andree Wagner, a Kaiserslautern fan who has studied Rehhagel's success closely, remembers the time well, and his description of their situation before and during the title success has uncanny similarities with Leicester's. They earned 33 points out of the next possible 42 up to December, but the title talk was still under wraps, allowing the team to go on without heightened publicity, further helped by Bayern and Dortmund's rocky starts to the campaign.
